claim: OpenAI's enforcement mechanism against heavy Codex subscription usage, following an April 9, 2026 update, is rate-limiting/quota throttling (e.g. 5-hour cooldown windows) rather than account suspension; affected users report cancelling subscriptions voluntarily due to unusable rate limits, not being banned.
stance_target: OpenAI suspends individually-owned Codex/ChatGPT subscriptions for high-volume automated usage the way Anthropic does
scope_conditions: OpenAI Codex CLI, April-May 2026, OpenAI Developer Community forum reports
quoted_support: I canceled my subscription because the new limit system is not a minor inconvenience -- it actively destroys development flow. Compared to the previous system, my productivity dropped by around 90%.

claim: No documented case of an individually-owned Codex/ChatGPT subscription account being suspended specifically for high automated-usage volume appears in this OpenAI Developer Community discussion; complaints center exclusively on rate-limit throttling frustration and voluntary cancellation.
stance_target: whether OpenAI, like Anthropic, suspends accounts for high-volume automated usage on individually-owned subscriptions
scope_conditions: OpenAI Developer Community forum thread on Codex CLI rate limits, 2026
quoted_support: This is also completely unusable for me. I am cancelling subscriptions as well. Waiting 5 hours every 3-4 small but complex due to the nature of my work, tasks, is completely unmanageable.
